X.rationale: X gives a narrow protocol-bounded hypothesis, patient-level estimand, fixed six-joint ontology, exact simple-first tensor interface, controlled-versus-natural panels, exhaustive ablation and leakage checks, paired analysis, prospective stopping rules, and an explicit DESIGN_ONLY boundary. Its main evidence-integrity weakness is that it requires receipt-bound execution and extensive artifact hashes without freezing the actual executor-receipt contract that will bind commands, raw outputs, completion state, and evaluation artifacts.

Y.rationale: Y is appropriately protocol-bounded, patient-level, ontology-faithful, leakage-aware, and explicit that it is DESIGN_ONLY. However, it leaves four load-bearing choices open: the exact primary endpoint and decision rule, the path-wise no_M0 neutralization contract, the ambiguity-stratum definition, and the shared training schedule. These unresolved choices reduce causal discrimination, statistical determinacy, comparator fairness, and reproducibility even though Y correctly blocks fitting until they are frozen.

winner_rationale: Round 1 totals are X=31 and Y=26 on the frozen Q1-Q8 scale, with no fatal defects recorded for either candidate. X therefore wins strictly by the higher total; the Round 2 findings do not alter that arithmetic rule.

findings.summary: X names receipt-bound execution and artifact hashes but does not specify the receipt object that proves which non-LLM execution produced which raw and evaluated outputs.
findings.locator: X, sections 8.12 Artifact binding, 10 First operational blocker, and 12 Truth boundary and proposed continuation decision.
findings.repair: Freeze a machine-verifiable executor-receipt schema before execution that binds run and command identity, source/environment/input/manifest hashes, start and completion state, exit status, raw-output hashes, checkpoint hashes, metric-code hash, evaluator-output hash, signer identity, signature, and independent verification result.

findings.summary: Y does not freeze the exact proper six-joint loss, possible macro co-primary, uncertainty procedure, or nonzero decision/equivalence margin, leaving the primary claim rule underdetermined.
findings.locator: Y, Falsifiable experiment > Primary outcome and Open and resolved conflicts > OPEN-PRIMARY-ENDPOINT-AND-DECISION-RULE.
findings.repair: Before any held-out outcome access, freeze one exact primary loss and direction, any co-primary status, patient-level aggregation, interval/test algorithm and parameters, missing-data rule, multiplicity rule, smallest-relevant-effect or equivalence margin, and a single deterministic continuation/falsification decision rule.

findings.summary: Y requires exhaustive M0 removal but leaves the path-wise neutralization rule open, so the intervention and its scale, missingness, capacity, and optimization parity are not yet reproducible.
findings.locator: Y, Implementable mechanism > Transformation and Open and resolved conflicts > OPEN-NO-M0-NEUTRALIZATION-CONTRACT.
findings.repair: Freeze the exhaustive direct-and-derived M0 path allowlist and, for every path, the normalized-space neutral value or masking/removal rule, state-support behavior, geometry handling, normalization source, parameter-opportunity policy, and byte-level metamorphic and tensor-diff acceptance tests.

findings.summary: Y makes cue-matched ambiguity strata load-bearing for mechanism discrimination but leaves their covariates, definitions, support thresholds, and analysis-versus-sampling use unresolved.
findings.locator: Y, Observable prediction, Distinguishing signal, and Open and resolved conflicts > OPEN-AMBIGUITY-STRATA-DEFINITION.
findings.repair: Using development/validation data only, freeze cue-visible covariates, binning or matching algorithm, distinct-patient support thresholds, unsupported-stratum handling, whether strata affect sampling or analysis, and the exact stratum-specific estimands before test access.

findings.summary: Y leaves staged versus flat training unresolved even though a shared exposure schedule is required to interpret full versus no_M0 as an access-only contrast.
findings.locator: Y, Falsifiable experiment > Held constant and Open and resolved conflicts > OPEN-SHARED-TRAINING-SCHEDULE.
findings.repair: Choose and hash one shared patient-first or flat schedule before fitting, including sampler, minibatch order, seed mapping, update budget, stopping, and checkpoint selection; keep any staged-versus-flat comparison as a separate development-only audit.

findings.summary: Y requires hashes and bundle closure but does not prospectively define how an executor receipt will bind commands, completion state, raw outputs, checkpoints, and blinded evaluation outputs.
findings.locator: Y, Stop condition, Open and resolved conflicts, and Truth boundary statement that producer identities and internal receipts are omitted.
findings.repair: Add a prospective receipt and verifier contract binding the frozen bundle and configuration to command identity, exit state, raw-result hashes, checkpoints, metric implementation, blinded evaluator outputs, signer identity, signature, and verification status without exposing producer identity in the blind rendering.

overall_notes: Round 1 scores and fatal-defect decisions were frozen before Round 2 defect auditing. Both candidates preserve the six-joint ontology, patient-level inference, leakage prohibitions, cross-attention deferral, and DESIGN_ONLY truth boundary; neither asserts results, runtime, novelty, model identity, cost, or publication readiness. Findings identify only packet-visible repair needs and do not imply that any experiment ran or that any statistical effect exists.
